definition: The standard subjective quality measures for synthesized speech: absolute 1-5 naturalness ratings (MOS) or side-by-side comparative ratings (CMOS).
details: The standard subjective quality measures for synthesized speech: absolute 1-5 naturalness ratings (MOS) or side-by-side comparative ratings (CMOS). Human MOS remains the gold standard; neural predictors (UTMOS-style) approximate it cheaply at scale.

explainer.lead: MOS and CMOS are the standard subjective quality measures for synthesized speech: absolute 1–5 naturalness ratings and side-by-side comparative ratings. Human MOS remains the gold standard.

tiers.eli5: People listen to computer speech and rate how natural it sounds, either on a 1–5 scale or by picking the better of two clips.
tiers.practitioner: Teams collect human ratings to judge speech synthesis and use neural predictors such as UTMOS-style models to approximate MOS cheaply at scale. The pitfall is treating predicted scores as a substitute for human listening.
tiers.paperLevel: Subjective 1–5 absolute naturalness ratings (MOS) and comparative side-by-side ratings (CMOS); human MOS is the gold standard, and neural predictors only approximate it cheaply at scale.

explainer.example: Listeners rate several synthesized clips from 1 to 5, and the average becomes the system's MOS.
